newsitem.title: FRANCE: Judge sends ex-French minister to trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge sends ex-French minister to trial.

text.p: A French judge on Monday ordered former industry minister Gerard Longuet to stand trial for suspected irregularities in the financing of his seaside holiday villa, justice sources said.
Investigating magistrate Mireille Filippini said Longuet, who quit the cabinet two years ago in a corruption probe, appeared to have benefitted from suspiciously generous credit terms.
Filippini decided to drop a separate case against Longuet involving suspicion of misuse of corporate funds in connection with a company he set up and later sold.
A centrist, Longuet is currently president of the elected council in the eastern region of Lorraine.

He was one of three ministers who resigned from the cabinet of ex-prime minister Edouard Balladur on suspicion of corruption in the run-up to 1995 presidential elections. Balladur stood in the election and lost to fellow-Gaullist Jacques Chirac.
